Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown leaf spots that darken; fruit may develop corky lesions and cracking.
Apple___Apple_scab.management: Remove fallen infected leaves and fruit; maintain canopy airflow; use locally approved fungicides when disease risk is high.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Use resistant cultivars where suitable, remove leaf debris, prune for airflow, and monitor early in the season.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-bordered leaf spots with tan centers; fruit develops brown rot and may remain mummified.
Apple___Black_rot.management: Remove mummified fruit and dead/cankered wood; improve orchard sanitation and use locally approved fungicides when warranted.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Prune dead wood, remove mummies and stressed plant material, and maintain tree vigor.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Yellow to orange-red leaf spots, often with darker structures; fruit can develop rough spots.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.management: Use resistant cultivars where available and manage the alternate cedar/juniper host when practical; fungicides may be used according to local guidance.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Avoid planting susceptible apple cultivars close to heavily infected cedar/juniper hosts where feasible and scout early.

Apple___healthy.management: No disease treatment is indicated from this classification alone; continue routine scouting.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain balanced nutrition, appropriate irrigation, sanitation, and regular scouting.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White-gray powdery fungal growth and distorted or curled young tissue may occur.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.management: Improve airflow and canopy light; remove heavily affected material where practical; use locally approved fungicides only when needed.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Avoid excessive canopy density and monitor susceptible new growth during favorable conditions.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Elongated gray to tan lesions, often becoming more noticeable on lower leaves and spreading upward.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.management: Use resistant hybrids where available; rotate crops and manage residue; consider locally recommended fungicide programs when disease risk warrants.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Crop rotation, residue management, resistant hybrids and timely scouting help reduce risk.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small reddish-brown to rust-colored pustules on leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.management: Use resistant hybrids and monitor fields; fungicide decisions should follow local disease risk and extension guidance.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Choose resistant varieties and scout during periods favorable for rust development.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: No characteristic disease symptoms detected by the classifier.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Use sound crop rotation, balanced fertility, irrigation management and scouting.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical gray-green to tan lesions that can enlarge and coalesce.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.management: Use resistant hybrids; rotate crops and manage residue; fungicides may be considered according to local risk and label directions.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Resistant hybrids, rotation, residue management and timely scouting reduce disease pressure.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf lesions may develop; berries can turn brown and become shriveled black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.management: Remove mummified berries and infected tissue; maintain canopy airflow and use locally approved fungicides when disease risk is high.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Sanitation, pruning for airflow and early-season scouting are important.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Leaf striping or spotting and fruit symptoms can occur; trunk disease may cause progressive decline.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).management: Remove or manage affected vines according to local vineyard pathology guidance; avoid spreading infected pruning material.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Use clean propagation material, sanitize pruning tools, and manage trunk wounds carefully.

Grape___healthy.prevention: Maintain canopy airflow, sanitation, balanced nutrition and regular scouting.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Leaf spots can enlarge and cause blighting or premature loss of foliage.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.management: Remove infected debris where practical; improve airflow and follow locally approved fungicide guidance if disease pressure is significant.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Canopy sanitation, airflow and regular scouting help reduce disease pressure.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Bacterium associated with Candidatus Liberibacter; spread by psyllids
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy leaf mottling, yellowing, twig decline and poor or misshapen fruit can occur.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).management: There is no simple curative treatment for an infected tree; confirm diagnosis with an appropriate diagnostic service and follow regional citrus HLB/vector management programs.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Use certified disease-free planting material and manage the vector according to regional recommendations.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked or dark leaf spots; fruit may develop sunken lesions.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.management: Use resistant/tolerant cultivars where available, improve sanitation and follow locally approved bactericide programs when warranted.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use healthy planting material, avoid unnecessary wetting of foliage, maintain orchard sanitation and scout regularly.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.management: Use disease-free seed/transplants, avoid overhead irrigation, rotate crops and follow locally approved copper/bactericide guidance when appropriate.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use clean seed/transplants, sanitation, crop rotation and avoid working plants when foliage is wet.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark leaf lesions often develop concentric rings; older leaves are commonly affected first.
Potato___Early_blight.management: Remove volunteer hosts and infected debris where feasible; maintain plant vigor and use locally approved fungicides when disease risk warrants.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Crop rotation, sanitation, balanced nutrition and regular scouting reduce risk.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: No characteristic disease symptoms detected by the classifier.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked or dark lesions can expand rapidly; humid conditions can promote sporulation.
Potato___Late_blight.management: Act quickly after confirmation; remove infected volunteer plants and follow local late-blight forecasting and approved fungicide programs.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Use certified seed, resistant/tolerant varieties where available, field sanitation and disease forecasting.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery growth develops on leaf surfaces and may lead to yellowing and premature leaf decline.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.management: Improve airflow and reduce plant stress; use resistant varieties where available and locally approved fungicides when needed.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Choose resistant cultivars, maintain airflow and scout regularly.

Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material, good drainage, sanitation and regular scouting.
sources: Penn State Extension — Plant Diseases and Control

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Small purple to reddish leaf spots enlarge and can cause scorched-looking foliage.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.management: Remove badly affected foliage when appropriate, improve airflow and follow local fungicide guidance if disease pressure warrants.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Use clean planting material, maintain airflow, avoid prolonged leaf wetness and remove infected debris.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Water-soaked spots develop on leaves and may turn dark; fruit can develop raised or sunken scabby spots.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.management: Use disease-free seed/transplants, avoid overhead irrigation, rotate crops and follow locally approved bactericide guidance.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use pathogen-free seed/transplants, sanitation, rotation and avoid handling wet plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark circular leaf lesions often show concentric rings; older leaves are commonly affected first.
Tomato___Early_blight.management: Remove affected lower leaves without excessive defoliation, keep foliage dry, improve airflow, rotate crops and use locally approved fungicides when warranted.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Use pathogen-free seed, crop rotation, sanitation, good airflow and regular scouting.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: No characteristic disease symptoms detected by the classifier.
Tomato___healthy.management: No disease treatment is indicated from this classification alone; continue routine scouting.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Maintain balanced fertility, irrigation, sanitation and regular scouting.
sources: Penn State Extension — Plant Diseases and Control

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions can expand rapidly, especially during cool, wet conditions.
Tomato___Late_blight.management: Treat as urgent after confirmation; remove infected material and follow local late-blight forecasting and approved fungicide programs.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Use healthy transplants, resistant/tolerant varieties where available, sanitation and disease forecasting.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow upper-leaf spots with olive-green to brown fungal growth commonly on lower leaf surfaces.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.management: Improve greenhouse/field ventilation and reduce leaf wetness; remove infected leaves and use locally approved fungicides if needed.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, sanitation, airflow and moisture management.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular leaf spots, often with dark margins and pale centers.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.management: Remove infected lower leaves and debris, avoid overhead irrigation, rotate crops and use locally approved fungicides when warranted.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Sanitation, crop rotation, good airflow and keeping foliage dry reduce risk.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine stippling/yellowing, webbing in heavier infestations, and leaf decline.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.management: Confirm mites before treatment; reduce plant stress, preserve beneficial predators, and use locally approved miticides only when thresholds justify treatment.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Avoid severe water stress, scout leaf undersides and conserve beneficial predatory mites/insects.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf lesions may develop concentric target-like rings; fruit lesions can occur.
Tomato___Target_Spot.management: Remove infected debris, improve airflow, avoid prolonged leaf wetness and use locally approved fungicides when warranted.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Sanitation, crop rotation, airflow and regular scouting reduce disease pressure.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mosaic or mottled light/dark green leaf patterns, distortion and variable growth reduction.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.management: There is no curative pesticide for an infected plant; remove confirmed infected plants and sanitize hands, tools and equipment to limit spread.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use clean seed/transplants, control contamination, sanitize tools and avoid handling plants when unnecessary.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Plant virus; commonly spread by whiteflies
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaf curling, yellowing, stunting and reduced fruit set can occur.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.management: There is no curative treatment for an infected plant; confirm diagnosis and manage whitefly vectors according to local IPM guidance.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, clean transplants and integrated whitefly management.
